questionText: In triangle $XYZ$, $x = 6\text{ cm}$, $Y = 70°$, and $Z = 55°$. Find the length of side $y$, correct to one decimal place.
markingScheme:
Find angle $X = 180° - 70° - 55° = 55°$ **(1 mark)**
Apply sine rule: $\dfrac{y}{\sin Y} = \dfrac{x}{\sin X}$ **(1 mark)**
Rearrange: $y = \dfrac{6\sin 70°}{\sin 55°}$ **(1 mark)**
Final answer $y \approx 6.9\text{ cm}$ **(2 marks)**

solutionSteps.explanation: Angles in a triangle sum to $180°$, so $X = 180° - 70° - 55° = 55°$.
We know a side $x$ and its opposite angle $X$, plus the angle $Y$ opposite the unknown side $y$. The sine rule gives $\dfrac{x}{\sin X} = \dfrac{y}{\sin Y}$.
